correctness.rationale: The explicit Gram dual X is positive semidefinite for m=p-1>=3, orthogonal to constants, has trace m+5=p+4, and gives squared distance exactly 1 on every allowed edge. Therefore tr(LX)=B for EVERY nonnegative edge weighting, yielding lambda2<=B/(p+4). The candidate with positive rates (leaf 2lambda, distinguished cross 3lambda/q, other cross lambda/q) has exact eigenvalue decomposition: eigenvalue lambda on A0 differences, lambda(p+2)/q on D differences, quotient eigenvalues lambda(0,1,t_plus,t_minus) with t_plus,t_minus>1 from the verified quadratic. Thus for q<=p+2 it saturates. If any allocation saturated above that threshold, automorphism averaging preserves its gap; complementary slackness against X forces the averaged candidate rates, whose D-difference eigenvalue is smaller. Contradiction. A separate six-vertex exact spectrum demonstrates failure of the same universal bound at p=3. Symbolic quotient identity and Gram equalities were replayed, with 57 exact rational graph cases and 189 independently assembled finite numerical spectral cases. None of the infinite steps relies on finite enumeration.

value.rationale: A complete sharp criterion identifies when a marginally attached vertex fixes the optimal continuous-time spectral gap regardless of opposite-part population. The exact ceiling B/(p+4), graph-independent dual Gram witness tight on every edge type, explicit 2:3:1 allocation, sharp q=p+2 exit threshold, and p=3 counterexample reveal nontrivial structural resource-allocation behavior. This is more than a renamed SDP, table recomputation or tiny numeric improvement: it supplies a directly usable design law and certificates for all p>=4 in the saturation region.
